newsitem.title: USA: Pentagon report blames lapses for Saudi bombing.
newsitem.headline: Pentagon report blames lapses for Saudi bombing.

text.p: The Pentagon on Monday said security lapses were partly to blame for American deaths in a bomb blast in Saudi Arabia in June and Defence Secretary William Perry urged greater vigilance to combat terrorism.

Perry called for "a radically new mind-set" to cope with the terrorist threat in a letter to President Bill Clinton accompanying Monday's Pentagon report on the June 25 truck bombing that killed 19 U.S. airmen in Dhahran, Saudi Arabia.

The report by retired Army General Wayne Downing said the military chain of command and the 4404th provisional wing, the Air Force unit policing a "no fly" zone in southern Iraq, had failed to take "all measures possible" to protect U.S. forces at the bombed Khobar Towers complex in Dhahran.
The investigation was ordered by Perry following the June 25 attack and another bombing which killed five Americans and two Indians last November 13 in Riyadh.

Perry, in his letter to Clinton, said "all of our leaders -- civilian and military -- must adopt a radically new mind-set with regard to international terrorism." He said the issue would be brought "front and center" as one factor to be weighed by the Pentagon when it considers how to carry out a deployment.

Downing's report did not recommend any disciplinary action in connection with lax protective or intelligence efforts prior to the bomb blasts, but Perry ordered the Air Force to examine the need for any discipline in the matter.
